_comment: Sources scripts/discover_jobs.py pulls from. Only public, unauthenticated ATS/career-site APIs -- nothing that requires login or violates a site's Terms of Service. Every company below was live-verified (a real HTTP request that actually returned postings) before being added, rather than guessed.
_smartrecruiters_note: The SmartRecruiters connector (scripts/discover_jobs.py: fetch_smartrecruiters_page / normalize_smartrecruiters_job) is implemented and tested, but api.smartrecruiters.com/v1/companies/{id}/postings only returns data for companies that have opted their public Postings feed in (SmartRecruiters disables it by default on lower plans). ~15 real companies were tried live (visa, bosch, tomtom, mcdonalds, ikea, adidas, skechers, docplanner, and more) and every one returned totalFound: 0. Add a company identifier here only once you've confirmed live (curl the URL above) that it returns non-zero postings.

_unavailable_sources.linkedin: Excluded by explicit decision -- LinkedIn does not offer the API access needed for general personal job discovery (no partner/Talent-Solutions agreement), and no unauthenticated bulk endpoint exists: robots.txt disallows /jobs-guest/ (the endpoint most no-login scrapers rely on) and /jobs?runSearch*, plus a blanket notice that 'automated means to access LinkedIn without express permission is strictly prohibited'.
_unavailable_sources.naukri: robots.txt explicitly names and blocks AI/LLM agents (Claude-User, claudebot, gptbot, etc.) with 'Disallow: /' -- this tool is directly named as disallowed, so it must not be accessed at all.
_unavailable_sources.indeed: robots.txt is largely permissive, but Indeed's Terms of Service separately prohibit automated scraping/data mining, and its public Job Search/Publisher API program (the only sanctioned bulk-access path) was closed to new applicants. Accessing search results programmatically without that partnership would mean ignoring documented anti-bot/ToS restrictions, which this project's access rules forbid.
_unavailable_sources.wellfound: robots.txt disallows /search and the job-listing query-param patterns (?jobId=, ?jobSlug=, ?role=) that any bulk discovery would need, and there is no public postings API. Individual static job pages exist but can't be enumerated without the disallowed search.
